## Pitcher's Perspective: When You Execute Your Gameplan

One game on the slate today, one result that went exactly as expected. From a pitcher's standpoint, that's what we call executing your pitch sequence—you identify the weakness, attack it, and get the out. The Braves were the play at 57% confidence, and they delivered.

## Breaking Down the Win

Phillies @ Braves was the only matchup, and it came down to what it always does in October baseball—pitching and execution. When I looked at this game, the 57% edge for Atlanta wasn't overwhelming, but it was there. In the postseason, you take your spots and trust your stuff. The Braves had the platoon advantage and home-field momentum. That's enough when you're locating your fastball.

## What Made the Difference

This wasn't about overpowering stuff or blowing anyone away. It was about reading the situation correctly. The Braves had the slight edge in the pitching matchup, they were playing at home, and they had the veteran presence to handle a divisional playoff atmosphere. When you're on the mound, you learn to trust those small edges—they add up over nine innings.

A 57% confidence pick means you're not guaranteeing anything. You're saying the odds favor one side, and today, those odds played out. That's all you can ask for in this game.
